primary_task: Report the health (launches, crash rate, unique users) of the latest published EAS Update group by running eas update:insights from the CLI.

requirements.name: eas-cli
requirements.basis: bash: "install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads)"

requirements.name: expo-account
requirements.basis: lacks: "accounts, logins, API keys or credentials for external services other than the listed connectors and GitHub (cloud providers such as AWS, Azure and GCP, SaaS products, model hubs, app stores, email delivery, payment)"

requirements.name: expo.dev
requirements.evidence: The data is the same data that powers the update and channel detail pages on expo.dev; these commands expose it in the terminal in human and JSON form.
requirements.basis: lacks: "network access to hosts outside the egress allow-list: only PyPI, npm, GitHub, Ubuntu apt archives, NuGet and the Go module proxy are open; other hosts are refused, for example huggingface.co, Microsoft Learn and Azure endpoints, Cloudflare, Expo, Neon and NVIDIA"; egress_deny lists "expo.dev" and "*.expo.dev"

requirements.name: jq
requirements.basis: bash: "install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, ...)"

requirements.name: expo-project-directory
requirements.evidence: For `channel:insights`: run from an Expo project directory (the command resolves the project ID from `app.json`). `update:insights` only needs a login.
requirements.basis: The manifest does not say what the working directory contains; check for app.json in the working directory.

notes: Took the representative request "Is the latest update healthy?" which needs eas update:list and eas update:insights; both need an Expo login and the Expo servers. jq is optional (only for filtering JSON). The feedback command (npx submit-expo-feedback) is optional. No reading makes this achievable: the data lives only on Expo's service.
